claim: The counter register is 24 bits but the expiry comparator only looks at the low 20 bits (WAIT's reach), so an exponent-3 DELAY with mantissa >= 32 ends early, the first time the count passes a multiple of 2^20.
spec_ref: docs/isa.md:Opcode table, DELAY row -- "cycles = mantissa << (exponent*5) ... exponent=3 -> up to ~16.7M (~335ms @ 50MHz)"; docs/architecture.md:Pipeline -- "DELAY stays in EXECUTE decrementing it until it hits zero (3+N cycles, N from the immediate)"

why_survives.directed: test_delay_exp3_full_counter_width (the rt01 fix) checks that the 24-bit count register loads N-1 and that DELAY 511<<15 has not ended within 100,000 cycles. Under the mutant the count loads correctly; DELAY 511<<15 (count 0xFF7FFF, low 20 bits 0xF7FFF) only ends early after ~1,015,807 cycles, beyond the 100k window. test_delay_timing uses exponent 0.
why_survives.random: Default DELAY is exponent 0/1 (<= 480 cycles); wide_timing's exponent-3 DELAY uses mantissa 1 (32768, fits 20 bits) and exponent-2 mantissa 1..4 (<= 4096).
why_survives.board: Firmware DELAYs and the I2C T_STRETCH timeout (32768) all fit 20 bits.
why_survives.formal: cycle_counter_timing_props is BMC depth 20; the first wrong expiry is >= 32768 cycles after load.
